A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same benchmarking study and retain the iPatch example. All 20 pages of v1 and 29 pages of v2, including appendices, provide readable text, tables, figures, and equations sufficient for comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original forecasting experiments across 14 datasets, hyperparameter-search stability experiments, and evaluations of iPatch, including detailed results in Appendix H.

after.justification: v2 retains original forecasting experiments and adds evaluated baselines, randomized ranking-sensitivity analysis, and computational-efficiency measurements.

M1.justification: iPatch retains cycle-based patching, successive variate and temporal attention, and the same MLP ordering (v1 Section 5.2; v2 Section 4.5). The added output-reshaping and channel-wise decoder description documents the existing architecture without establishing an algorithmic change.

E1.justification: Forecasting coverage remains the same 14 datasets across five domains, with horizons 96, 192, 336, and 720. The benchmark-diversity audit and synthetic-input efficiency profiling do not add forecasting datasets or task requirements.

E2.justification: S-Mamba, xLSTMTime, and ModernTCN join the main comparison and the comparison with iPatch. Appendix H adds ARIMA and LOCF, labeled CLOF in Tables 12–13. The ranking-sensitivity comparisons also include TimeMixer, which was absent from v1's corresponding exclusion plots.

E3.justification: v2 replaces selected dataset/horizon exclusions with 5,000 uniformly sampled subset configurations. It introduces efficiency metrics and a composite score, with profiling over 1,000 synthetic-input iterations at batch size one. New baseline settings include MAE loss for xLSTMTime and a separate ModernTCN width grid. The original models' 40-trial search budget and documented grids are retained.

E4.justification: The limited exclusion examples in v1 Sections 4.1–4.2 become a systematic ranking-sensitivity analysis in v2 Section 4.1. v2 also adds an audit of benchmark diversity by domain, sampling frequency, and variate count, plus performance–efficiency analyses with and without MotorImagery. The earlier dataset-pattern, PCA, and HP-search stability analyses are retained.

E5.justification: v2 adds score distributions and plus/minus summaries across sampled benchmark configurations. It replaces v1's all-pairs sign-test reporting with a focused iPatch–iTransformer comparison and explicitly reports the expanded Friedman comparison for MAE. Three final training seeds, the two-search stability check, and the underlying Friedman/sign-test procedures remain unchanged.

E6.justification: New baselines and efficiency measurements substantially expand the results. Existing scores also change: in Table 2, TimeMixer's horizon-averaged Exchange MSE changes from 33705.21 to 0.550, and PatchTST's BeijingAir MSE from 0.8643 to 0.578. iPatch's Exchange results are revised in Appendix H. These are revised reports, with their causes undocumented, rather than established same-setting performance gains. The expanded comparison also changes aggregate rankings and Friedman results.

T1.justification: Section 4.6 introduces the mathematical definition of the composite efficiency-weighted score ξ, including baseline normalization, metric directionality, weighting, and calibration reasoning. The existing iPatch mathematics, dataset-statistic definitions, and statistical-test formulas remain substantively unchanged; no new theorem or proof is added.

C1.justification: The central claims that no model consistently dominates and that benchmarking needs greater rigor are retained. The title, abstract, introduction, and conclusion now explicitly restrict these claims to supervised LTSF, with foundation models excluded from the empirical claim's scope.

C2.justification: v2 adds substantive interpretations concerning insufficient benchmark diversity, computational costs of architectural complexity, and simple baselines' competitiveness on Exchange. Section 6 adds concrete limitations concerning fixed horizons across domains, sensitivity to implementation and search choices, and the exclusion of foundation models. These extend v1's shorter alternative-view discussion.

D1.justification: v2 replaces the promise of a future code release with a stated repository location. It documents additional baseline settings, iPatch decoder details, and the efficiency-profiling procedure and hardware, including an RTX 4090 and AMD EPYC processor. Most original preprocessing and HP-search information is retained or relocated.

R1.justification: v2 substantially expands its positioning as independent confirmatory research, adding literature on unreliable benchmarking across machine-learning fields. It incorporates GIFT-Eval, additional architecture families, and more extensive discussion of foundation-model and LLM forecasting limitations. These are substantive additions beyond bibliographic publication updates.

P1.justification: The narrative is extensively reorganized and rewritten. Dataset-guided model selection moves from v1 Section 6 into v2 Section 3; the statistical-testing and iPatch material moves into Section 4.5; HP details are consolidated in Appendix C. Recommendations and limitations become substantially revised dedicated sections.

P2.justification: The two-column conference presentation becomes a predominantly single-column journal layout. New benchmark-diversity and ranking-distribution figures accompany expanded radar and violin plots. Tables are restructured, mean and minimum full results are separated, efficiency tables are added, and the old pairwise-win matrix is removed. Boxed model summaries and recommendations further change the presentation.

improvement.justification: v2 substantially strengthens the evidence behind the benchmarking critique: broader architectural and simple-baseline comparisons address v1's restricted comparator coverage, while 5,000 sampled configurations replace a few selected exclusion examples. Section 4.6 and Appendix I quantify computational trade-offs that v1 explicitly left outside scope. Clearer applicability limits and code-access information also improve the paper. Unexplained score revisions and substantial reproduction gaps for ModernTCN and xLSTMTime in Table 9 remain weaknesses, but the broader, more diagnostic evidence provides a substantial net improvement.
